name: US federal tax: Internal Revenue Code, Treasury regulations, IRS guidance, Tax Court
_doc: Shipped as the second worked example, so that 'packs are pluggable' is a demonstrated claim and not a promise. It is also the body of law a founder is most likely to be arguing about. Load ALONGSIDE us-federal.
_official_domains: Merged into the review grounding by `krokai review`; teaches the lookalike detector the names worth impersonating (`irs.com` is a live commercial site that is NOT the agency).

aliases._doc: IRC § 162 IS 26 U.S.C. § 162 — the same provision under two names, exactly like INA/8 U.S.C. No map is needed because the section numbers are identical; only the title prefix is added. Absence of a `map` key means pass the captured value straight through.

shapes._what: Treas. Reg. § 1.162-4 — the part number is what precedes the first dot (here, 1).
Rev. Rul. 99-6 / Rev. Proc. 2024-12 — published IRS guidance.
shapes.sample: the treatment in Rev. Rul. 99-6 controls

shapes._what: 142 T.C. 1 / T.C. Memo. 2019-134 — Tax Court. Recognised as a neighbour citation; the address of a case is its party names, which us-federal supplies.

PLR 202412008 — a private letter ruling. 🔴 Recognised on purpose so that the report can show it, because IRC § 6110(k)(3) says it may not be used or cited as precedent. Seeing it in a draft is the point.
